attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter, stated in his voice.

semantics.note: The causal allegation is preserved. Limiting it to tech workers matches the surrounding text. The normalised version leaves out 'liars', which also alleges they knew the claims were false, but the contract keeps that element.

contract.note: The plain reading (widespread, materially higher mental-health harm among tech workers, caused by knowingly false capability claims) is the ordinary reading of firm words. The bar is demanding, but it follows from what he asserted. No threshold or baseline is given.

evidence.note: One-company study reporting strain and intensified work. It neither measures an epidemic nor ties the strain to the named leaders' statements.
ILO paper naming psychosocial risk mechanisms such as surveillance and intensification. Says nothing about causation by the alleged lies.
Sponsored cross-industry survey: 62% of AI users say their burnout fell. This is a company disclosure and a different population, so it cautions against the claim but does not settle it.

reviews.rationale: No representative evidence in the packet establishes an epidemic among tech workers in June 2026, or links harm to knowingly false claims by Altman, Amodei or their backers. Nothing rules it out either: the Workday survey is sponsored and covers another population. The evidence does not settle the claim.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion in his newsletter.

semantics.note: The normalised version keeps the investee-lab exclusion and 'meaningful'. 'Of any kind' is softened slightly but the scope is kept.

contract.note: Reading 'meaningful' as commercially substantial revenue from customers other than investee labs is ordinary. The evaluator picked Q1 2026 as the period, which is reasonable. Requiring revenue broken out by customer sets a high evidentiary bar but is not unfair.

evidence.note: Microsoft: over 20M paid Copilot seats, and Copilot named as a driver of ARPU growth. Points against the claim, but gives no standalone realized AI revenue figure.
Alphabet: AI credited for Search growth, and Cloud up 63% led by enterprise AI. Neither AI revenue nor its customer mix (Anthropic is an investee) is broken out.

reviews.rationale: Both disclosures point to sizeable AI-linked business outside the investee labs: paid Copilot seats and enterprise AI driving Cloud growth. Neither gives realized AI revenue with investee customers excluded, as the contract requires. They weigh against the claim, but the packet does not settle it.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in a sidenote about Meta.

semantics.note: A firm present-tense denial that Meta's GPUs cause meaningful ad-revenue gains. Classing it as causal fits.

contract.note: Reading it as a denial of material incremental ad revenue is ordinary. Using Q1 2026 and requiring attribution against a counterfactual are reasonable. 'Meaningful' has no threshold.

evidence.note: Meta reports conversion-rate gains (6%+, 1.6%) from GPU-backed ad models. This is management's own attribution and an advertiser-side metric, not incremental revenue to Meta.
October 2026 engineering post that ties the GEM ads model to GPU training. Later period, and no revenue measure.

reviews.rationale: Meta's disclosures report conversion improvements from GPU-trained ad models, which cuts against the claim. But the packet has no credible attribution of incremental Q1 2026 ad revenue in either direction. Under the contract the claim remains unresolved.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his newsletter.

semantics.note: 'Not going to' is a firm forecast. Treating the 'only revenue' estimate as a separate claim is acceptable. 'Fulcrum to adding' is rendered roughly as 'produce', which is close enough.

contract.note: No deadline is stated, and the contract treats 'digital God' as untestable, which is fair. Its definitions of recursive self-improvement and the revenue limb are reasonable. The early-resolution rule allows only contradiction.

evidence.note: September 2026 preprint on recursive improvement of agent software with the models held fixed, run on A100s. It is not tied to the specified GPU fleet and is not a decisive event.

reviews.rationale: The forecast has no deadline. The preprint does not meet the early-resolution rule: it is not attributable to H100/B200/B300 deployments and is not a verified self-improvement event of the kind defined. No $600B revenue measurement exists. Non-occurrence so far cannot support the forecast, so it stays open.
